To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the probability of pore forming in an ultrathin amorphous carbon film by an ion with a sufficiently large charge is very low and that it decreases with the increase in the ion charge.

the probability of pore creation by multicharged Xe+q (q = 20–53) ions with energies of ~50 keV incident on a carbon film is 0.1–0.5% for the case when the ion beam is normal to the film surface and 1–5% for the grazing incidence case.

the probability of pore creation by multicharged Xe+q (q = 20–50) ions with energies of ~50 keV incident on an ultratthin carbon film is calculated using a quantum-mechanical approach and that it is shown that the probability of the formation of pores in the film is related to the probability of perforation of the film by the moving ion wave packet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of nanometer-sized holes in a carbon film by the impact of multicharged ions with energies of 40–100 keV.
the problem of pore formation in a carbon film by the passage of a multicharged Xe+q ion.
the development of a theory for the propagation of multicharged ions through an ultrathinfilm, with a particular emphasis on the formation of a pore.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a xenon ion of charge q ≥ 20, the probability of pore creation in the film is close to unity.
the probability of pore creation by a moving multicharged ion is very low and can be estimated by the formula P ∼ (q/100)2.
the formation of a pore is due to the action of a multicharged ion with a sufficiently large charge and kinetic energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of pores by multicharged ion impact on ultrathin films is a stochastic process, which depends on the charge state of the ion, its kinetic energy, and the thickness and density of the film.
the probability of pore forming is determined by the ratio of the ion charge q to the charge state of the ion q0 at which the ion is able to pass through a pore.

the formation of a pore in a carbon film is a result of the interaction between the ion and the film, and the pore is formed as the ion moves through the film, and not because of a preexisting defect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probability of pore creation can be calculated from the ion charge and the energy deposited in the film.
the probability of pore perforation increases as the charge of the incident ion increases.
the probability of pore creation can be estimated from the ratio of the number of atoms in the ionized wave packet to the number of atoms that form a pore.
